objective: Find every way, as of October 2026, for commits made in claude.ai cloud (Claude Code on the web) sessions to show Verified on GitHub on feature branches too, and how the session can take the user's real git identity from the GitHub connector without storing it in the repository.
scope: Root probe facts (2026-10-27, this claude.ai cloud session): mcp__github__get_me returns login, id 39467981 and name but no email; commits created through the GitHub MCP connector (push_files, create_or_update_file) carry author David Basile Filho <davidbasilefilho@gmail.com> and are unsigned (verification.reason unsigned); the session's GitHub proxy blocks GraphQL entirely and REST git/trees, git/commits and contents writes with HTTP 403; git push to the session branch works; CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=cloud_default are set; git comes preconfigured as Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>.

Search Anthropic docs (code.claude.com, docs.claude.com, support.claude.com), the claude-code GitHub issues and changelog for commit signing, verified commits, git identity, author email in cloud sessions, and the environment settings (secrets, setup script) that could hold an SSH signing key.

Identity: where the user's email can come from without a repository file (connector, GitHub noreply form <id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com, environment variables, git config set at session start in .git/config which is not committed), and whether GitHub verifies a signed commit whose author is the noreply email.

Signing: SSH signing key in environment secrets (setup script can or cannot read secrets), gpg.format ssh, whether git push through the session proxy keeps signatures, and any built-in Anthropic signing feature.

Look up facts that may have changed (product features, versions, release assets) with the Exa tools instead of answering from memory, and cite each source URL or file:line.

result:
result: In this session git CLI commits are already configured to be signed through Anthropic's signing service as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`, so they should already show Verified on any branch. Only the MCP/API commits are unsigned. No route yields Verified commits authored and committed as the real user without putting a user key inside the VM. I did not test an actual commit here; that is the first thing the root should do.

changed: none
checks: none run (read-only research; no shell). Local files read: `/root/.gitconfig`, `/etc/gitconfig`, `/root/.ccr/README.md`.
blockers: none. The Exa tools worked despite the authentication notice.
questions: Does the user have GitHub vigilant mode on? That decides Verified versus Partially verified in routes 2 and 3 below.

**Routes to Verified commits on feature branches (documented sources: S1, S2, S3, S7, S9)**

1. **Default git CLI commit, author and committer both `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`**
   - Mechanism: git signs through Anthropic's signing service, with a `/tmp/code-sign` shim via `gpg.format=ssh`. Signatures are verifiable against Anthropic's published SSH key.
   - Setup: nothing. The root should use `git commit` rather than the MCP `push_files` or `create_or_update_file`.
   - Security cost: none. The key stays outside the VM.
   - Status: SOURCED.
     - `/root/.gitconfig` in this session shows `commit.gpgsign=true`, `gpg.format=ssh`, `gpg.ssh.program=/tmp/code-sign`, and `user.signingkey=/home/claude/.ssh/commit_signing_key.pub` (exists).
     - S3 says commits are signed as Claude and Verified (a user report from 2026-10-23, not an official page).
     - S2 gives the self-hosted equivalent of this config.
   - Not confirmed here: `/tmp/code-sign` did not exist when I looked, and the root has not tested a commit. A signature is part of the commit, so it persists across branches and pushes (S5). The proxy blocks only branch deletions and non-branch refs (S1). Whether pushes keep the signature is inference, but the proxy relays the git objects.

2. **Real user as author, Claude as committer (`git commit --author` or `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`)**
   - Mechanism: the committer stays Claude, so the signature verifies. Env vars override the git config author (S8).
   - Setup: set the author env vars per command; do not touch committer.
   - Security cost: none.
   - Status: SOURCED.
     - S3 says Verified when vigilant mode is off, but "Partially verified" when the author has vigilant mode on. S5 says the same.
     - S6 reports a contradicting experience: author env vars gave an "Upload your public signing SSH key" error. This probably came from also overriding the committer or signing key; the cause is inference.
   - Open: the author email must carry the user's email, or the noreply ID form, to link the commit to the account (S4).

3. **Claude as author, with a `Co-authored-by: <id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` trailer**
   - Mechanism: the signature is Claude's, so the commit is Verified even with vigilant mode on. The user is credited by the trailer.
   - Setup: add the trailer to the commit message.
   - Security cost: none.
   - Status: the trailer is SOURCED as an existing pattern (S2: the self-hosted runner hook adds it from `CCR_SESSION_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`; S6 requests it for hosted sessions). The Verified result is inference from route 1, since the trailer does not affect the signature.

4. **User's own SSH signing key stored in the environment**
   - Mechanism: set `user.signingkey` and `gpg.ssh.program` back to plain ssh-keygen, and upload the public key to GitHub as a Signing Key. Author and committer are then the real user, with an email verified on the account.
   - Setup: generate the key, upload it to GitHub, put the private key in the environment, and write it to disk at session start.
   - Security cost: high.
     - Environment variables and setup scripts are readable by anyone who uses the environment (S1).
     - Network secrets cannot carry it, because they are only attached to HTTP requests for listed hosts (S1).
     - The setup script runs before environment variables are set, and network secrets are never attached to setup-script requests (S1). A key therefore cannot reach the script from secrets, only be pasted in the script itself, which is also readable.
     - S3 calls the environment-secret route unsafe for a shared environment.
   - Status: the key-upload mechanics are SOURCED (S9 for the pattern, S5 for GitHub). Applying it to cloud sessions is INFERENCE; no source shows anyone doing it.

5. **Committer set to the user's email while still signing with Anthropic's key**
   - Expected result: Unverified (`bad_email`) because the key's owner differs. This is INFERENCE from the reason-code table in S10 (a secondary source) and S5's rule that the committer is the verification target. Not recommended.

6. **Not available as of 2026-10-27**
   - Per-user signing in the Claude app with the key held server-side: requested in S3 (open, 2026-10-23).
   - Server-side signing through a GitHub App API for cloud sessions: requested in S7 (open, labelled stale).
   - SOURCED: both issues are open. I found no changelog or doc announcing either.

7. **GitHub-API commits (MCP/REST)**
   - Status: not a route.
     - The root probe shows these are unsigned.
     - The proxy blocks REST `git/commits` and `git/trees`.
     - S5 says GitHub signs for bots only when no custom author or committer is supplied. That condition applies to bot tokens, and the unsigned result for the user's connector token matches it. This is INFERENCE.

8. **Self-hosted environment with `--configure-git`**
   - Mechanism: the same Anthropic signing service, or your own git config shipped in the runner image.
   - Status: SOURCED (S2). Not applicable to the hosted environment this session uses.

**Identity sources that avoid a repository file**

| Source | Yields | Status |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub connector `get_me` | login, id 39467981, name; no email | Root probe |
| GitHub noreply form `<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` (accounts created after 2017-07-18) | Constructable email from `get_me` data; links commits to the account, and survives username changes (S4) | SOURCED |
| Author email on an existing MCP-created commit, via `get_commit` or `list_commits` | Name and real email (`davidbasilefilho@gmail.com`) | Root probe; reading it at runtime is inference |
| Env vars `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` (set per command) | Overrides the git config author | SOURCED (S8). Note S8 also reports an Anthropic-shipped SessionStart hook, `~/.claude/session-start-git-identity.sh`, rewrites the global config and can race other hooks, so env vars are more robust than `git config --global`. |
| `git config --local` in `.git/config` at session start | Name and email, untracked | The untracked file is general git behaviour (inference). The global-config race in S8 applies here too. |
| Environment variable in the environment settings | Any value | SOURCED (S1), but readable by all users of the environment, not a repository file |
| `CCR_SESSION_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`, or the session JWT `act.email` claim | The session creator's email | SOURCED for self-hosted only (S2, S11). Hosted tokens use the `sk-ant-si-` prefix, and I found no doc saying either value is set in hosted sessions. |

**Noreply author and verification:** GitHub evaluates the committer email against the signing key owner (S5, S10). With Anthropic's key, only the committer must be `noreply@anthropic.com`. A noreply author does not break verification. I found no GitHub source saying a user-noreply committer with a user key fails or succeeds; for route 4 I infer it verifies if the key is on that account.

**Sources (consulted 2026-10-27; S1, S2 and S5 are official docs)**
- S1: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web
- S2: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-deploy (Configure git section)
- S3: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104719 (open, 2026-10-23)
- S4: https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/reference/email-addresses-reference
- S5: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification and https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/displaying-verification-statuses-for-all-of-your-commits
- S6: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/18715
- S7: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/90255 and https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/7711
- S8: https://github.com/coo-labs/coo-harness/issues/427 (third party, 2026-06-04)
- S9: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/9a3c761f/docs/security.md
- S10: https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3756681.3756959 (secondary, reason-code table)
- S11: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-identity

**Conflicts and limits:** S6 conflicts with S3 on author overrides, as noted under route 2. The Claude Code changelog was not fetched. Nothing here is from after 2026-10-27.

notes:
- Verification test for the root: make a scratch commit with `git commit` (with and without `--author`), push it, then check `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification`. REST is allowed through the proxy; GraphQL is not.
- If `/tmp/code-sign` is absent when the session commits, signing will fail and the commit will error rather than be unsigned.
